t: You're on Victoria Embankment, a road and river-walk along the north bank of the Thames. It runs from the Palace of Westminster to Blackfriars Bridge, was built in the 1860s, and takes its name from Queen Victoria. Its designer was Sir Joseph Bazalgette, chief engineer of London's Metropolitan Board of Works. After the Great Stink of 1858 he created the main drainage system for central London, which helped relieve the city of cholera. Inside the embankment runs the low-level Northern Outfall Sewer, carrying sewage away instead of into the river, along with part of the District Line.
